subject: Accounting for bilateral symmetry in 3D GMM results in 2D graphics

messages.author: f885e974e72cf61d
messages.subject: Accounting for bilateral symmetry in 3D GMM results in 2D graphics
parts:
Hi Geomorph community,

Like many others here, I am a novice at geometric morphometrics, R, and Geomorph, but I follow this group closely and have not seen other posts pertaining to my question. As such, I would greatly appreciate your insights. 

My master's project is looking at patterns of brain shape variation in Mustelidae (the weasel family) using 3D GMM. Since brains have object symmetry, I thought it would be appropriate to account for this in my analyses (the two hemispheres are rarely identical, though). However, when I use the output from bilat.symmetry to run a PCA, the data is depicted in 2 dimensions instead of 3. Using the gpagen output without bilateral symmetry does not do this. Is this supposed to happen? Am I running an incorrect analysis or running analyses in the wrong order? Details and code below, images attached.

Each specimen has 34 landmarks and 234 sliding semilandmarks. It is my understanding that to incorporate semilandmarks into the bilateral symmetry analysis, a GPA should be performed first. That is what I have done. In case this was a snafu on my part, I tried running bilat.symmetry with the raw data (NTSdata) and still receive the same result.


Code:

mustelid.gpa = gpagen(A=NTSdata, curves = slidinglmks, surfaces = surfacelmks,
                    PrinAxes=TRUE, ProcD=FALSE, Proj=TRUE, print.progress=TRUE)

mustelid.data = geomorph.data.frame(shape = mustelid.gpa$coords, ind=EcoTable$R_ID)
mustelid.sym = bilat.symmetry(A=shape, ind = ind, object.sym=TRUE, land.pairs = bilateralsymmetry, 
                  data=mustelid.data, RRPP = TRUE, iter = 999, print.progress = TRUE)

PCA with bilateral symmetry:
PCA=plotTangentSpace(mustelid.sym$symm.shape, axis1 = 1, axis2 = 2, warpgrids = TRUE, verbose = TRUE, label = EcoTable$CommonName)
summary(PCA)

PCA without bilateral symmetry:
PCA=plotTangentSpace(mustelid.gpa$coords, axis1 = 1, axis2 = 2, warpgrids = TRUE, verbose = TRUE, label = EcoTable$CommonName)
summary(PCA)


Does anyone have any ideas as to what is going wrong or what I am doing incorrectly? Should I conduct all of my analyses without accounting for bilateral symmetry?
Thank you, and I look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,
Ani Hristova
